advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether an open scope should re-close on a matching success and, if so, clear `opened` in _ScopeState.reset() (or document the latch explicitly).
evidence: `def reset(self) -> None:` sets only `self.consecutive = 0`, `self.tickets = set()`, `self.endpoints = set()` (pass_fuse.py:76-80) and leaves `self.opened` untouched

record() success path calls `self._endpoint_state(...).reset()` / `self._provider_state(provider).reset()` (pass_fuse.py:105-108) but decision_for returns `provider_state.opened` / `endpoint_state.opened` regardless (pass_fuse.py:155-162)
module docstring: 'A matching success resets that scope\'s consecutive run.' and test docstring 'A matching success ... resets that scope' — but an OPENED scope never re-closes
advisory.finding: _ScopeState.reset() does not clear `opened`, so a matching success cannot actually close/reset an already-open scope — decision_for keeps returning the open FuseDecision for the rest of the pass, contradicting the documented 'a matching success resets that scope' contract.
scenarios: An endpoint opens (3 eligible / 2 tickets), then a genuine success on that endpoint arrives later in the same pass; decision_for still reports the endpoint as open.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat an unresolved (None) provider/endpoint binding as an explicit non-eligible/skip-with-signal rather than silently folding all unknowns into one shared scope.
evidence: `binding: Mapping = self._locate(identity) or {}` then `return binding.get("provider"), binding.get("endpoint")` (pass_fuse.py:93-95) — a missing key silently yields None with no signal
coordinator default `_empty_locate` returns `{}` for every identity (coordinator.py:127-128), so an unconfigured locate makes ALL identities collapse to (None,None)
_endpoint_state/_provider_state key on these values (pass_fuse.py:97-102), so unrelated unknown identities share one scope
advisory.finding: _resolve() maps an unresolvable/empty locate() binding to (provider=None, endpoint=None) and folds it silently into a single shared scope, so identities whose (provider,endpoint) cannot be resolved are invisible — distinct unknown-binding tickets accumulate together toward the endpoint threshold and can spuriously open the (None,None) fuse, or a miss is never surfaced as an error.
scenarios: locate is the default/empty or a binding is missing a key; three eligible outcomes across two unrelated unknown identities open a bogus (None,None) endpoint fuse.
A misconfigured locate silently produces no fuse for genuinely failing endpoints — the fuse's absence of a decision is indistinguishable from 'binding never resolved'.

blocking.finding: No test covers a matching success arriving AFTER a scope has opened. `_ScopeState.reset()` (pass_fuse.py:79-82) deliberately omits `opened`, so `record()`'s success branch (pass_fuse.py:109-112) resets counters but leaves an already-open scope open; `decision_for` still returns the stale decision. Every reset test (test_matching_success_resets_consecutive_state, test_provider_reset_on_success_clears_distinct_endpoints) resets BEFORE the threshold is reached, so the sticky-vs-clearing behavior of a post-open success is never pinned.
merged_from: No test asserts that `decision_for` prefers the OPEN provider scope over an OPEN endpoint scope for the SAME identity. The precedence branch (pass_fuse.py:158-163) returns the provider decision first, but test_decision_fields_are_exact only checks T-3 (whose endpoint b never opened) for the provider scope; it never asserts that T-1 — whose endpoint a IS open and whose provider then opens — flips from an 'endpoint' decision to a 'provider' decision.
